description:
What a budget buys in 2-3 towns or cities: the share of each place's
    active listings within the price cap, and optionally also with parking.

    Use when the user compares places by what they can afford ("2-bed flats
    up to 300k in Porto or Valencia", "and with parking?"). For each place it
    counts the cohort (type, sale, bedrooms), the part within `max_price`,
    and, with `has_parking`, the part within budget whose listing mentions
    parking. `share_pct` is that part over the place's priced cohort.

    Relay the SHARES, not the counts: counts reflect how many listings Cubi
    holds for each place, not the size of the market. These are asking
    prices of active listings, not sale prices or valuations; say so. A
    place is counted at the level in `level` (a city when the name has a city
    reading). Never compute or invent a figure that is not in the result.

    Args:
        places: 2-3 town or city names, e.g. ["Porto", "Valencia"].
        type: property types, e.g. ["apartment"].
        transaction_type: "sale" (default). Rental budgets are not supported.
        min_bedrooms / max_bedrooms: bedroom bounds (equal for "exactly 2").
        max_price: asking-price cap in EUR.
        has_parking: also count the budget cohort with parking mentioned.
        lang: ISO 639-1 code for the sample listings (en/pt/es/fr/de/nl/ru).

    Returns:
        JSON: places[{place, level, base, within_budget, with_parking, listings}],
        each cohort {count, priced, on_request, share_pct}; `listings` are up
        to 3 homes from the last cohort counted, for "show me those".
name: compare_inventory
title: Compare what a budget buys
